addSheet.byoFollowup: Hostname is still validated via DNS-TXT. After it goes live, upload your certificate via the per-domain Replace action below.

methodHints.dns_txt: Default. Operator adds a TXT record at _astrolift-challenge.<hostname>.
methodHints.http_01: ACME HTTP-01 challenge served from the cluster's ingress controller. Pick this when DNS edits are slow.
methodHints.dns_01: ACME DNS-01 challenge. Required for wildcards and zones where ACM / cloud cert manager handles the records.
methodHints.byo_cert: Skip ACME entirely. Validate via DNS-TXT, then paste your own PEM chain + private key.

addSheet.title: Add custom domain
addSheet.description: The platform issues a cert via Let's Encrypt once the DNS validation record is in place.

domains.title: Custom domains
domains.description: Hostnames bound to {slug}. Add a domain, copy the validation TXT record into your DNS provider, then click Recheck once it propagates.
domains.emptyDescription: Add a hostname like checkout.acme.com to point at this app's primary public workload. Removing a domain later detaches it from ingress — the platform stops routing traffic for that hostname and the cert is freed.

remove.title: Remove {hostname}?
remove.description: Soft-deletes the app↔hostname binding. The cert is freed and the hostname becomes available to re-add to another app. The DNS record at your provider is unaffected.

cert.platformManagedHelp: Platform-managed records — astrolift owns the zone and creates these via the DNS driver. No operator action needed; the recheck below is a probe.
cert.liveHelp: These records are live in your DNS. Cert active.
cert.needsHelp: Add these records to your authoritative DNS, then click Recheck. The platform queries your zone's nameservers directly so propagation typically takes < 5 min.
cert.allPropagated: All records propagated. Validation should flip to validated on the next workflow tick (or click Recheck to force one).
cert.noHandshake: Handshake not generated yet — re-add the domain to refresh its required records.
cert.issuingPlatform: DNS-01 challenge in progress with the cloud cert manager.
cert.issuingExternal: HTTP-01 challenge running against your CNAME target.
cert.activeDesc: Serving HTTPS for {hostname}. The renderer picks the cert up automatically on the next deploy.
cert.byoNote: The platform won't auto-rotate this cert. Re-upload before its expiry to avoid a service interruption.
cert.failedHelp: Common causes: external DNS zone on AWS (ACM can't HTTP-01), Let's Encrypt rate limit on the apex, or the CNAME isn't reachable on port 80. Upload your own certificate to bypass auto-issuance, or fix the upstream cause and click Recheck.
cert.queued: DNS validated. Certificate issuance queued — should start within a minute. If it doesn't, click Recheck to retrigger.

upload.title: Upload certificate for {hostname}
upload.description: Paste the full PEM-encoded certificate chain (leaf + any intermediates) and the matching private key. The platform stores the bundle and projects it as a Kubernetes TLS Secret on the runtime cluster on the next deploy. Replaces any in-flight auto-issuance.
upload.certInvalid: Doesn't look like a PEM CERTIFICATE block.
upload.keyInvalid: Doesn't look like a PEM-encoded private key.
upload.noRotate: The platform won't auto-rotate this cert. Track its expiry yourself; re-upload before it lapses to avoid a service interruption.

ingress.maintenanceDesc: Every bound hostname is returning 503. Health probes that hit ingress will fail; in-cluster probes are unaffected.

webhookDeploys.title: Webhook deploys
webhookDeploys.description: App-global pause for CI / push / scheduled deploys. Manual deploys from the UI or CLI keep working so you can still ship a fix.
webhookDeploys.scopeNoteLive: Webhook-fired deploys (push, CI, scheduled) accept normally. Pausing stops all three; manual deploys remain available.
webhookDeploys.scopeNotePaused: Webhook-fired deploys refused. Manual deploys, rollbacks, promotions, and teardown remain available.
webhookDeploys.confirmTitle: Pause webhook deploys for this app?
webhookDeploys.confirmDescription: Future deploys from CI, push events, and cron will be refused until you resume. Manual deploys from the UI or CLI continue to work.

forceRedeploy.title: Force redeploy
forceRedeploy.description: Recovery for a wedged app. Cancels in-flight deploys, deletes the per-workload Kubernetes objects, and re-fires the CI deploy workflow. Brief downtime while the rollout window opens.
forceRedeploy.buttonTooltip: Recovery for stuck deploys. Cancels pending deploys, deletes K8s objects, and re-fires the deploy workflow. Brief downtime while pods recreate.
forceRedeploy.hint: Use only when a normal redeploy can't unstick the app — e.g. orphaned k8s objects after a rename or a deploy row that won't reconcile.
forceRedeploy.confirmDescription: This cancels any pending deploys, deletes the app's running Kubernetes objects (Deployments, Services, Ingresses, CronJobs), and re-fires the CI workflow. Live traffic drops briefly while the rollout window opens. Environments with required approvals still go through the approver flow.
